chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man for whom some of his children are more beloved to him than others, and he places some of his children before others. He said: 'Yes, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) did that, bestowing upon Muhammad. And Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did that, bestowing something upon Ahmad, so I arose with him until I obtained it for him.'

So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What about a man for whom his daughters are more beloved to him than his sons?' He said: 'The daughters and the sons are equal in that; it is merely according to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends down for them from Him.'

key_terms.نَحَلَ: to bestow a gift or endowment
key_terms.يُنَزِّلُهُمُ: He sends down for them (divine decree/portion)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a father to give more gifts to one child over another in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of a father showing preference among children in gifts (nahla), citing the precedent of Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Kazim. It clarifies that while gender does not inherently dictate preference, the ultimate distribution is governed by divine decree (qadr), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that parental discretion is valid but rooted in God's wisdom.
